title: Generation of interspecies mouse-rat chimeric embryos by embryonic stem (ES) cell microinjection
protocol: Sacrifice the plugged donor females by cervical dislocation.
Anesthetize rats with 4% isoflurane before sacrificing.
Collect early embryos from either mouse or rat.
Prepare collected embryos for microinjection with ES cells of the respective other species.
Dissect out the Fallopian tubes and place them in a Petri dish containing M2 medium.
Flush the embryos out of the oviducts using a needle attached to a syringe.
Inject M2 medium directly into the ampulla of mouse oviducts to flush embryos.
Rupture rat oviducts with fine forceps and a 27G × ¾” needle before flushing.
Use a syringe to flush the embryos out from ruptured rat oviducts with M2 medium.
Collect flushed embryos by mouth-pipetting using a custom-made pipetting device equipped with a handling capillary.
Transfer collected embryos to a fresh Petri dish filled with M2 medium.
Fill the handling capillary with M2 medium and introduce an air bubble.
Wash isolated embryos 10 times in drops of M2 medium (100 μl per drop).
Pick all healthy 8-cell embryos by mouth pipetting using a custom-made pipetting device equipped with a handling capillary.
Transfer embryos from the first drop of M2 medium to the second drop, filling the capillary with fresh M2 medium and introducing an air bubble before each transfer.
Clean or change the handling capillary after transferring all embryos to the next drop of M2 medium.
Repeat the transfer steps until all embryos have been moved through 10 drops of M2 medium.
After the embryos have been washed, move all of them to 200 μl of KSOM medium in a Petri dish.
Cover the KSOM medium with paraffin oil.
Incubate the isolated embryos in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 / 95% air at 37°C.
Aspirate the culture medium from the ES cell culture dishes/plates.
Wash the ES cells with 1 ml of pre-warmed PBS per 10-cm dish or per well of the 12-well plate.
Aspirate the PBS and add chicken serum with 0.1% trypsin (1 mL per 10-cm dish or well of the 12-well plate).
Incubate for 7–8 min in a cell culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 / 95% air.
Resuspend the trypsinized cells in ES cell culture medium and centrifuge for 5 min at 123 × g.
Aspirate most of the supernatant, leaving about 500 μL medium for resuspending mouse ES cell pellet.
Aspirate the supernatant completely and add 500 μL of 2i medium to resuspend rat ES cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet with gentle shaking and store on ice until microinjection (maximum 4 h).
Inject embryos of the recipient species with ES cells from the other species to generate chimeric embryos.
Fill the microinjection chamber with HEPES-buffered ES cell culture medium.
Place a vertical strip of ES cells from the single-cell suspension into the microinjection chamber using a mouth-pipetting device equipped with a handling capillary.
Position the ES cells on the side where the collection capillary or injection needle manipulator is located.
Clean the handling capillary.
Place embryos (10–12 per batch) in the chamber opposite to the ES cells.
Inject the embryos in batches of 10–12 embryos per batch to avoid prolonged incubation under unfavorable conditions.
Replace ES cells in the microinjection chamber with fresh ES cells for subsequent batches.
Collect 80–100 ES cells into the collection capillary/injection needle, ensuring minimal gaps between cells.
Attach an 8-cell stage embryo to the holding capillary of the microinjection system, positioning a blastomere-free region away from the holding site.
Insert the injection needle through the zona pellucida into the perivitelline space in a region devoid of blastomeres by piercing manually.
Deliver a tangential laser pulse for 640 μs at 64% power to the outer margin of the zona pellucida.
Insert the injection needle through the laser-created puncture.
Inject 8–10 ES cells into the embryo slowly.
Gently withdraw the injection needle after injecting the ES cells.
Transfer microinjected embryos to a 200-μL drop of fresh KSOM medium in a 3.5-mm cell culture dish.
Cover the KSOM medium with paraffin oil.
Place the dish in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 / 95% air at 37°C in the cell culture incubator.
Transfer embryos into pseudo-pregnant fosters on the same day as microinjection.
Wash the microinjected chimeric embryos 5–6 times in consecutive 100 μl drops of M2 medium to remove any traces of KSOM medium.
Move the washed embryos to a new sterile Petri dish containing M2 medium.
Collect the embryos by mouth-pipetting into a transfer capillary.
Fill the transfer capillary with a small amount of M2 medium.
Introduce an air bubble into the transfer capillary.
Collect 6-8 chimeric embryos per unilateral oviduct transfer into a rat foster.
Collect 11-13 chimeric embryos per unilateral transfer into a mouse foster.
Prepare pseudo-pregnant (E0.5) foster females for oviduct transfer surgery.
Anesthetize the animal using intraperitoneal injection of ketamine/xylazine/acepromazine mixture.
Administer continuous inhalation of 2.5%-4% isoflurane with 0.4-0.8 L/min O2 flow during surgery.
Place the animal on its back and wait for loss of righting and palpebral reflexes.
Apply protective cream to the animal’s eyes to prevent drying.
Set the operating table or heating pad to maintain 37°C.
Keep the animal on the operating table or heating pad throughout surgery and anesthesia recovery.
Administer metamizole subcutaneously, 10 minutes before surgery if using isoflurane (200 mg/kg body weight).
Shave the hairs around the operating region with a razor blade.
Clean and disinfect the skin at the shaven site with 70% ethanol.
Make a 0.8–1 cm long incision with 11-cm fine scissors to open the skin and abdominal cavity at the shaven area.
Expose the oviduct proximal to the ovary by gently pulling out the fat pad.
Fix the fat pad with a bulldog clamp.
Locate the infundibulum and the ampulla.
Check for a swollen ampulla and the presence of a corpus luteum in the ovary.
Insert the transfer capillary containing the embryos into the ampulla through the infundibulum.
Transfer the embryos from the transfer capillary into the ampulla using gentle pressure by mouth-pipetting.
Recognize a successful transfer by the presence of an air bubble inside the ampulla.
Slowly remove the capillary.
Gently place the oviduct back into the abdominal cavity, in its original position.
Expose the oviduct on the other side for bi-lateral transfers and repeat the procedure.
Close the peritoneum by suturing with sterile surgical sutures.
Close the skin using 9-mm metal Autoclips.
Move the operated animal to a fresh cage.
Monitor the animal during recovery from anesthesia.
Keep the animal warm using infrared light or a heating pad under the cage.
Monitor the animal for recovery from anesthesia until it shows no signs of pain and starts moving freely.
Provide post-operative pain treatment with metamizole at 1.33 mg/mL in drinking water for two days post-operation to foster females after surgery.
Place operated foster females in a calm and quiet environment during recovery.
Avoid opening the cage to minimize disturbance to the animal.
Weigh and examine foster mothers periodically for signs of pregnancy after mid-gestation without daily disturbances.
Remove metal clips carefully with a clip remover (Agnthos, Clip Remover, 59026) when the skin has healed, typically 5 days post-operation.
Place the E0.5 pseudo-pregnant foster females under isoflurane anesthesia using continuous inhalation of 2.5%–4% Isoflurane with a 0.4–0.8 L/min O₂ flow.
Apply protective cream to the animal’s eyes to prevent drying.
Set the operating table or heating pad to maintain 37°C.
Shave the hairs around the operating region on the dorsal side, parallel to the mid-line and close to the ovary position for oviduct transfers with a razor blade.
Clean and disinfect the skin at the shaven site with 70% ethanol.
Place the rat foster female in the prone position under isoflurane anesthesia.
Clean and shave the operated area on the back of the animal with ethanol.
Make an incision through the skin to expose the abdominal cavity containing the ovary and oviduct.
Use forceps to pull away fat tissue to access the oviduct, keeping the anesthesia mask in place.
Perform a close-up incision exposing the oviduct, identifying the ovary, oviduct, and fat pad with colored arrowheads.
Insert a transfer capillary into the ampulla of the oviduct for embryo transfer.
Close the skin incision with metal clips placed closely together to prevent wound opening.
Make a 2.5-cm long incision with fine scissors in the shaven area on the skin and peritoneal wall.
Expose the oviduct by gently pulling out the fat pad from the region proximal to the ovary.
Fix the fat pad using a bulldog clamp.
Locate the ampulla and infundibulum of the oviduct.
Open the ampulla with an acupuncture needle.
Insert the transfer capillary directly into the ampulla through the opening made by the needle.
Transfer embryos from the transfer capillary into the ampulla using gentle pressure by mouth-pipetting.
Apply a few drops of warm PBS onto the oviducts and nearby organs if the transfer takes more than 10 minutes to avoid drying.
Remove the capillary from the ampulla slowly.
Gently place the oviduct back into its original position in the abdominal cavity.
Do not apply pressure to the oviducts when placing them back into the abdominal cavity.
Expose the oviduct on the other side for bi-lateral transfers and repeat the procedure.
Suture the peritoneum with sterile surgical sutures (Ethicon, Vicryl, P3, USP 5-0, 45 cm).
Close the skin using 9-mm metal Autoclips (Agnthos, 59023 and 59024).
Move the operated animal to a fresh cage after surgery.
Monitor the animal during recovery from anesthesia until it shows no signs of pain and moves freely.
Keep the animal warm with infrared light or a heating pad under the cage during recovery.
Provide post-operative pain treatment (metamizole 1.33 mg/mL in drinking water) for two days post-operation to foster females.
Monitor foster females regularly for signs of pain over the next few days.
Avoid opening the cage to minimize disturbance and stress for the animals.
Periodically weigh and examine foster mothers for signs of pregnancy after mid-gestation.
Remove metal clips from the skin of foster females carefully when it has healed (typically 5 days post-operation).
Shave hairs around the operating region with a razor blade.
Clean and disinfect the shaved area with 70% ethanol.
Perform surgery to transfer chimeric embryos into uterine horns of pseudo-pregnant foster females.
Open the skin and peritoneal wall at the shaven area by making a 1-cm long incision with 11-cm fine scissors.
Expose the uterine horn region about 6–8 mm distal to the end of the oviduct.
Hold the end of the uterine horn using fine blunt-end forceps.
Make a hole into the uterine wall using a 27G × ¾” needle (Braun Omnifix, Luer Lock).
Insert the transfer capillary containing the embryos into the uterine horn through this opening.
Transfer the embryos from the transfer capillary into the uterine horn using gentle pressure by mouth-pipetting.
Slowly remove the transfer capillary from the uterine horn.
Apply a few drops of warm PBS onto the uterus and nearby organs if the transfer takes more than 10 min.
Gently place the uterine horn back into the abdominal cavity in its original position.
Expose the uterine horn on the other side for bi-lateral transfers.
Repeat the procedure to expose, hold, make a hole, insert embryos, transfer embryos, remove capillary, and apply warm PBS as necessary.
Close the peritoneum by suturing with sterile surgical sutures.
Close the skin using 9-mm metal Autoclips.
Move the operated animal to a fresh cage and monitor it during recovery from anesthesia.
Keep the animal warm using infrared light or a heating pad under the cage.
Monitor the animal throughout recovery for signs of pain and movement.
Provide post-operative pain treatment with metamizole in drinking water for two days.
Monitor foster females regularly for signs of pain without disturbing them.
Avoid housing rat foster females singly to minimize stress.
Sacrifice the pregnant foster females by cervical dislocation or anesthesia followed by cervical dislocation.
Dissect the uteri and open them using surgical scissors to collect developing embryos.
Check for pregnancy status and live embryo presence if necessary.
Genotype tissue and organ samples by PCR to detect chimerism.
Collect small samples of tissues and organs during embryo dissection for genotyping or freeze them until use.
Isolate DNA from the collected samples using isopropanol extraction.
Use multiple primer pairs in PCR reactions to distinguish cells from two species.
Amplify DNA with rat-specific primers, mouse-specific primers, EGFP-amplifying primers, and gender-specific primers.
